A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 21 pages of v2 and 26 pages of v3 support comparison, including figures, equations, proofs, and appendices. Retained hyperparameter and architecture appendices can be matched despite renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 report original toy experiments and neural-representation evaluations on DSprites, MPI3D, and Shapes3D, using 36 architecture/loss configurations per dataset.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds runtime measurements and bin-count and sample-size sensitivity results in Section 5.3 and Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: The proposed mutual-information ratios, maximization and averaging rules, and discretization-based estimation procedure remain unchanged. The theoretical revisions and clarified sub-representation terminology do not introduce a new algorithm or model component.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 extends synthetic evaluation to settings with 2–20 generative factors, beyond the four-factor toy comparison reported in v2. The dependent-factor and nuisance scenarios and the three named image benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator set remains FactorVAE, MIG, SAP, Modularity, and DCI's Disentanglement and Completeness. The new timing comparison groups the latter two as DCI; this does not introduce a different comparator.

E3.justification: V2 states that all experiments use 15 bins; v3 specifies 20 bins for Figure 2. V3 adds sweeps over 10–30 bins and 1,000–10,000 samples, plus runtime evaluation. The neural training grid and 1,000-sample classifier protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 adds systematic discretization and sample-size sensitivity analyses for both toy experiments and the neural-representation evaluations in Appendices B–C. Section 5.3 additionally tests computational scaling with the number of factors. These substantial robustness and feasibility analyses are absent from v2.

E5.justification: The new runtime plot in Figure 4 introduces shaded bands around timing curves. Their statistical meaning and repetition counts are not specified, so no particular confidence-interval procedure or increase in repeated runs can be established.

E6.justification: Figures 2–3 revise the toy-result curves, while Figures 4 and 7–16 add substantial runtime and sensitivity results. New findings include lower Min-Suf runtime than MIG and Modularity and largely stable key downstream correlations across sample counts. The changed discretization precludes interpreting revised toy curves as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 changes from an equivalence to the one-way implication that minimality entails factors-invariance and nuisances-invariance; Appendix A removes the converse proof. Section 3 also removes the assumption that factors are conditionally independent given the input. Theorem 2 is retained.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the claimed if-and-only-if characterization with a connection between the four properties and minimality/sufficiency, substantially narrowing a central theoretical contribution. This revision is incomplete: the abstract and Section 4.2 still retain equivalence claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds the explanation that separate invariance checks can miss joint factor–nuisance effects and notes the scarcity of nuisance labels. New Section 8 identifies non-differentiability and poor high-dimensional discretization scalability, with proposed future remedies.

D1.justification: V3 newly specifies 5,000 samples for Figure 2, explicitly states the need for ground-truth factor labels, and clarifies joint computation of Minimality and Sufficiency. Existing training and architecture tables are retained. The same repository link moves from a footnote to Code Availability.

R1.justification: V3 adds Kraskov et al. (2004), Xu et al. (2020), and Almudévar et al. (2025b) to support future estimation and optimization directions, and removes the Predefined Prototypes reference. Most other citation changes update publication metadata without changing research positioning.

P1.justification: V3 adds explicit notation conventions, makes localized explanatory rewrites, and inserts scalability, limitations, sensitivity-analysis, and code-availability sections. Most existing prose and the main narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds eleven figures: one runtime comparison and ten appendix sensitivity figures. It also redraws toy plots, relocates the neural-result plots, revises captions and legends, and adopts publication headers. The twelve hyperparameter and architecture tables are retained.

improvement.justification: The added sensitivity and runtime analyses strengthen the empirical assessment, and narrowing Theorem 1 removes its previously claimed converse. Clearer limitations also improve interpretation. These gains are limited by the incomplete theoretical correction: the abstract and Section 4.2 still assert equivalence, and the new timing bands remain statistically undefined.
